capabilities.label: Analytics report
capabilities.description: Read-time observations over retained evidence and operational services, with scoped contributors and private saved definitions.

capabilities.label: Business partner
capabilities.description: One record per company or person you trade with. Roles such as customer or supplier are stated on the partner, not by keeping two address books. Delivery holds and pricing groups attach here.

capabilities.label: Item
capabilities.description: The operational identity of a product with its unit. Stock is never stored on the item; it is derived from movements and reservations at read time, which is why the stock lists live here.

capabilities.label: Warehouse location
capabilities.description: A physical or logical place. Only stock-capable locations can hold goods; a hierarchy is expressed through the parent location.

capabilities.label: Prices and payment terms
capabilities.description: The commercial conditions an order or invoice is judged against. Price resolution shows which list applies to which partner; payment terms drive due dates and early payment discounts.

capabilities.label: Order
capabilities.description: A promise to deliver or to receive: Reality calls it a commitment. The order document is evidence; open quantity, ship readiness and delays are derived from the commitment, its reservations and the movements that fulfil it.

capabilities.label: Delivery and goods receipt
capabilities.description: Every physical change of stock is an append-only movement; corrections add a compensating movement instead of editing. A shipment is the consignment that carries movements to or from a counterparty, with carrier observations attached.

capabilities.label: Lot, serial number and pallet
capabilities.description: A lot or serial unit identifies a subset of an item; a handling unit identifies a pallet by its NVE/SSCC. Best-before dates are stated by someone who read them, never computed.

capabilities.label: Invoice and credit note
capabilities.description: Recording an invoice stores the evidence; booking it posts the ledger entries. Open items compare what was billed with what was paid or credited, per partner and currency.

capabilities.label: Payment and settlement
capabilities.description: A payment is evidence with a balanced posting behind it. Allocating it to invoices or credits is the settlement; a short payment is accepted as an agreed deduction or left open. Payment runs pay suppliers in bulk. Public payment reads filter direction only as incoming or outgoing; customer or supplier is a party-balance side, not a payment direction.

capabilities.label: Ledger and accounts
capabilities.description: The balanced journal every posting lands in, the operational accounts it uses, and the configuration that maps postings to an external accounting system. Reversals add an inverse posting group; nothing is deleted.

capabilities.label: Contribution margin
capabilities.description: The explainable bridge from received net revenue through reviewed consumed acquisition cost to DB1, and through direct and allocated selling costs to DB2. Missing evidence stays unknown; every confirmed result retains its review and knowledge boundary.

capabilities.label: Return
capabilities.description: A return is announced, arrives as a goods receipt, is decided on, and ends in a credit or refund. Each step is its own record, so a return that stalls between two steps is visible.

capabilities.label: Document and source system
capabilities.description: Everything Reality knows arrives as an immutable source record from a system, a file or a person. Documents are the normalized evidence; a fact is one stated observation about an existing record. Interpretation failures and silent sources surface as exceptions.

capabilities.label: Company and users
capabilities.description: Who may work in a company and how far its data has been set up. Every business record is scoped to one company; another company's records behave as not found.

capabilities.label: Approvals, exceptions and open questions
capabilities.description: An agent never changes business state directly: it proposes, a person approves, and the proposal executes through the same command a clerk would use. Exceptions are the derived attention queue; missing information collects questions the records cannot answer yet.
